clue.text: See union member's revolting hairdo

indicators.note: revolting means turning over, so the letters of the whole string are read from the back

parts.note: to see a difference is to tell it
M is the abbreviation for member, as in MP

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a trade unionist's dreadful haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: TELL, U and M together give TELLUM, which 'revolting' turns round. Like many down answers here, it is also a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A mullet is the haircut short at the front and long at the back, a notoriously unfashionable style.

clue.text: Some barbershop arrangements for consort

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some close-harmony arrangements suit a group of singers or players.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'for consort' as the definition; 'for' is only a link word, and the definition is 'consort' alone. Catherine Parr was Henry VIII's sixth wife; a parr is also a young salmon.
explanation.definitionFit: Catherine Parr was queen consort to Henry VIII, the last of his six wives.

clue.text: Easy for one in military intelligence having compromised Danish PM

parts.note: MI stands for Military Intelligence, as in MI5

indicators.note: compromised means damaged or put out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spy story: an easy target in the intelligence services has exposed the Danish prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Easy' looks like an adjective but is a name: Mr Midshipman Easy is the hero of Captain Marryat's 1836 novel. The rearranged letters of DANISH PM give DSHIPMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Easy, title character of Marryat's novel, holds the junior naval rank in question, so he is an example.

clue.text: A stretch of picturesque alfalfa grass

indicators.note: A stretch of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A scenic expanse of a fodder crop, alfalfa, is itself a kind of grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' pretends to be a plant beside alfalfa, but here it is the verb meaning to inform on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang verbs for informing on criminals to the police.

clue.text: Boot from the foot of Miss Minola?

indicators.note: in a down clue the foot is the bottom, so the last letter of Miss is taken

parts.note: Kate Minola is the shrew of Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew

explanation.surface: Asks whether a boot came off Katherine Minola's foot in Shakespeare's comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: S, the last letter of 'Miss', comes before KATE, the first name of Katharina Minola. A skate is also a flat fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice skate is a boot with a blade fixed under it.

clue.text: Giddy girl has endless champagne before concert

indicators.note: before places the champagne part ahead of the concert part
endless says the final letter is cut from the word for champagne

parts.note: fizz is slang for champagne
a gig is a concert, especially of pop music

explanation.surface: A young woman sips bubbly before going to a gig.
explanation.walkthrough: A fizgig is an old word for a flighty, frivolous girl.
explanation.definitionFit: The old word describes a flirtatious, flighty young woman, which is what a giddy girl is.

clue.text: Indignation after making the first daughter good bait for those down here

indicators.note: after making X good means X has been changed into the letter for good

parts.note: dudgeon is resentment or indignation, as in 'in high dudgeon'
D is the abbreviation for daughter; the first of the two Ds is the one changed

explanation.surface: An angler's indignation has turned into a good bait, once a daughter's interference is fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'those down here' are the down answers, most of which are fish: mullet, parr, skate, groper, minnow, blenny, loach, carp and so on. DUDGEON has two Ds; only the first becomes G.
explanation.definitionFit: The gudgeon is a small freshwater fish traditionally used as live bait for pike and other predators.

clue.text: Greek guy, for instance, admitted he likes to cop a feel

definitions.text: he likes to cop a feel

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the rope goes inside the Greek abbreviation

parts.note: a guy is a rope holding a tent or mast, so it is an example of a rope

explanation.surface: A man from Greece confessed to being a handsy pest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' reads as a man, but it is a guy rope. The answer is also a large fish of warm seas.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who touches others sexually without consent; to cop a feel is to grope.

clue.text: Number of tunes, very avant-garde

indicators.note: avant-garde means experimental and unconventional, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A collection of highly experimental songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a song in a list of tunes, but here it means a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Seventy-four is an integer, so it is an example of a number.

clue.text: Poet in shopping centre toting gun, sawn-off at the end

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre

indicators.note: sawn-off at the end says the final letter of the word for gun-toting is cut

parts.note: someone toting a gun is armed

explanation.surface: An armed gunman with a sawn-off shotgun in a shopping mall.
explanation.walkthrough: Stéphane Mallarmé was a French Symbolist poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Mallarmé was a leading nineteenth-century French Symbolist writer of verse.

clue.text: Nerdy types plug in special operating system

indicators.note: in places the advertisement inside the other letters

parts.note: DOS is a disk operating system, as in MS-DOS
a plug is an advertisement, shortened to ad

explanation.surface: Geeks plug a cable into an unusual computer system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plug' suggests an electrical plug; it is a piece of promotion. Saddo is British slang for a pathetic, socially inept person.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddo is a dull, socially awkward person, close to a nerd or geek.

clue.text: Holy man diving into river is nuts

indicators.note: diving into puts the saint inside the river's name

parts.note: the Tees is a river in north-east England
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A clergyman plunging into a river is mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' reads as crazy, but is slang for testicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts is slang for the male reproductive glands.

clue.text: Cut interest accruing to money

indicators.note: accruing to means being added on after, so the interest follows the money

parts.note: silver is coins, so money
an interest is a group or party with shared concerns, so a side

explanation.surface: A banking line: cut the interest that builds up on savings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a verb about reducing interest; it is a joint of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Silverside is a joint of beef from the outer thigh, used for salt beef: a butcher's cut.

clue.text: Poor devil gets charged by detective with a malevolent look

indicators.note: charged means filled, so the rearranged letters are filled with the detective
poor means in bad shape, so the letters of devil are rearranged

parts.note: a private eye is a detective

explanation.surface: An unfortunate rogue is arrested by a detective with a nasty look on his face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges DEVIL to EVILD, and 'gets charged by' fills it with EYE, a private eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The evil eye is a glare believed to cast harm, so an evil-eyed look is a malevolent stare.

clue.text: Dance fan ordered one meatball

indicators.note: ordered means put in a fresh arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dance enthusiast asked for a single meatball at a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A balletomane is an enthusiast for ballet, a devotee of that theatrical dance form.

clue.text: Old local woman encapsulates English women in a sentence

indicators.note: encapsulates means holds within, so the two letters go inside A LIFE

parts.note: a life sentence, or life, is a prison term

explanation.surface: An old woman in the area describes English women in one sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is a pub. EW goes inside A LIFE after the L. The answer is also a fish of the herring family.
explanation.definitionFit: An alewife was a woman who kept an alehouse, an old term for a pub landlady.

clue.text: Doctor goes round boozer with someone of no significance

indicators.note: goes round says the doctor's letters surround the pub

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
boozer is British slang for a pub, here an inn

explanation.surface: A GP visits a pub accompanied by a nobody.
explanation.walkthrough: A minnow is also a tiny freshwater fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A minnow is figuratively an unimportant person or small player, like a minor team in a cup.

clue.text: Fine veal could be stuffed in this

definitions.text: Fine veal could be stuffed in this

indicators.note: stuffed suggests being crammed and mixed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cookery note: good veal might be wrapped inside this.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the letters of FINE VEAL rearranged spell the wrapper itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Grape-vine foliage is used as a wrapper for fillings, as in Greek dolmades.

clue.text: Central point on foreign island is attractive

parts.note: the nub is the central point or crux
île is French for island

explanation.surface: The heart of an overseas isle is appealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Nubile describes a young woman who is sexually attractive; the sense is close to alluring.

clue.text: Swimmer's speed when crossing lake

indicators.note: crossing means lying across, so the drug's letters straddle the lake letter

parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine, and a benny is a Benzedrine pill

explanation.surface: A swimmer's pace as they cross a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speed' looks like velocity, but it is the drug. A blenny is a small fish of rocky shores.
explanation.definitionFit: A blenny is a small spiny-finned fish, and fish are swimmers.

clue.text: Film director gets part of spliff that's changed hands

indicators.note: changed hands means the right-hand letter is swapped for the left-hand one

parts.note: the roach is the cardboard filter end of a cannabis joint

explanation.surface: A film-maker is given a joint's butt that's been passed around.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Loach is the British director of Kes and I, Daniel Blake. 'changed hands' swaps R (right) for L (left). A loach is also a freshwater fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Ken Loach is a celebrated British maker of social-realist films.

clue.text: Opposed to Conservative's capers

parts.note: anti means against
the 's of Conservative's supplies S

explanation.surface: Against the Tory's pranks.
explanation.definitionFit: Capers and antics are both playful or silly pranks: plural synonyms.

clue.text: Can mules wander freely in America?

indicators.note: letters that wander freely move about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks whether mules may roam at liberty in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Sam is the personification of the United States government and nation.

clue.text: Complain about a BBC accent

parts.note: C is short for circa, about
RP, Received Pronunciation, is the standard accent once heard on the BBC

explanation.surface: Grumbling about the posh way BBC presenters speak.
explanation.walkthrough: RP, Received Pronunciation, is the prestige British accent. A carp is also a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to find fault or grumble persistently.

clue.text: Write all day on a regular basis? That's manageable

indicators.note: regular means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Is writing all day, every day, something you can cope with?
explanation.walkthrough: Wieldy is the rare positive of unwieldy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wieldy is easily handled or controlled, the opposite of unwieldy.

clue.text: Steep run impedes English actress

indicators.note: impedes means gets in the way, so the run sits in the middle of the actress's name

parts.note: Dame Judi Dench is an English actress
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A steep run blocks Judi Dench's path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steep' reads as an adjective for the run, but is the verb meaning to soak.
explanation.definitionFit: To steep something is to soak it thoroughly in liquid, as with drench.
